newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has expressed skepticism over the Constitution Drafting Assembly's proposal to determine who would become prime minister based on results of the proportional representation election. The CDA's proposed election system would mix constituency elections with proportional representation. (THE NATION)

- Plans by the military to spend five billion baht on armoured vehicles project and an estimated one billion baht on light tanks could be realised in the next fiscal year. The Budget Bureau, which has stalled the procurement plans as part of the government's austerity programme, has changed its mind after the Defence Ministry calls for a halt to the delay. (BANGKOK POST)

- The 1998 Bangkok 13th Asian Games have been pushed deeper into the mire as an embattled Major General Charouck Arirachakaran has threatened to quit as director of the events organisation committee. Charouck, sacked by the Cabinet as the secretary of the Bangkok Asian Games Organising Committee (BAGOC) on Thursday, has fired verbal volleys at Deputy Prime Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol, the chairman of BAGOC. (THE NATION)

- The merger of seven finance and securities firms is expected to take until November to complete, executives say. The group, led by CMIC Finance and Securities Plc and Nava Finance and Securities Plc, hopes to establish a new commercial bank later. The merger will not necessarily result in layoffs of staff at any of the seven companies involved. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Expressway and Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (ETA) appears to be on the hook to pay one billion baht in compensation to the contractor of its 25 billion baht Bang Na-Bangprakong expressway to cover interest and other additional expenses resulting from an 11-month delay in handing over the construction site. (THE NATION)
